journal_name: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology

abstracts.abstract: Knowledge graph completion remains a fundamental challenge in intelligent systems due to the inherent limitations of traditional embedding-based approaches in capturing symbolic reasoning patterns. This paper proposes NeuroSymbolicKGE, a novel paradigm that integrates neural network representations with symbolic reasoning mechanisms for knowledge graph embedding. Unlike conventional methods that rely solely on statistical learning from entity and relation embeddings, our framework introduces a differentiable logic layer that enables explicit rule extraction and symbolic inference over the knowledge structure. We formalize this hybrid architecture as a tensor decomposition framework augmented with first-order logic constraints, where neural components model confidence scores while symbolic components enforce logical consistency. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets including FB15k-237 and WN18RR demonstrate that our paradigm achieves significant improvements in link prediction tasks, particularly for complex multi-hop reasoning scenarios. The proposed approach achieves 10.2% improvement in Hits@10 compared to state-of-the-art embedding methods while providing interpretable reasoning paths. This work establishes a new research direction that bridges the gap between statistical learning and knowledge representation, contributing to the advancement of AI technology in knowledge discovery applications.

Graph neural networks have demonstrated remarkable performance in recommendation systems by modeling complex user-item interactions as heterogeneous graphs. However, existing approaches suffer from over-smoothing and representation saturation when aggregating information across multiple hops, limiting their effectiveness in capturing long-range dependencies. This paper introduces AdaptiveDepth-GNN, a novel graph neural architecture with depth-adaptive aggregation mechanisms specifically designed for recommender systems. Our method employs a learned gating mechanism that dynamically controls the information flow at each layer, enabling the model to automatically determine the optimal receptive field for different user-item pairs. We theoretically analyze the gradient flow properties and prove that our architecture alleviates the over-smoothing problem through a novel residual-like connection strategy. Experiments conducted on three real-world datasets (MovieLens-1M, Amazon-Book, and Last-FM) show that our method consistently outperforms baseline approaches, achieving a 7.8% improvement in Recall@20 and 12.3% improvement in NDCG@20. The proposed framework maintains computational efficiency while significantly enhancing the model's ability to capture both local and global interaction patterns in web intelligence applications.

The proliferation of social media platforms has generated unprecedented volumes of multimodal content, necessitating intelligent systems that can effectively analyze cross-modal information for real-time event detection and sentiment analysis. This paper presents SocialScope, a comprehensive intelligent analytics platform that integrates text mining, visual analysis, and social network modeling within a unified framework. The system architecture comprises three novel components: (1) a cross-modal fusion engine leveraging contrastive learning for aligning textual and visual representations; (2) a dynamic knowledge graph construction module that extracts entities and relationships from social media streams; and (3) an adaptive inference engine employing large language models enhanced with retrieved knowledge for contextual understanding. We design an end-to-end pipeline that processes over 10,000 posts per minute with sub-second latency using distributed computing架构. Extensive deployment experiments across three major social media platforms demonstrate the system's effectiveness in detecting emerging topics with 94.3% accuracy and identifying sentiment trends with 91.7% F1-score. The platform provides real-time dashboards and API interfaces for intelligent agents, contributing significantly to social media intelligence applications and supporting data-driven decision-making in crisis management scenarios.

Personalized recommendation in e-commerce environments faces critical challenges in handling sparse user behavior data and cold-start problems for new items. Existing recommender systems often struggle to incorporate rich contextual information and semantic relationships between products. This paper presents ContextGraph-Rec, an improved recommender system architecture that enhances graph-based recommendation through enhanced context awareness and semantic enrichment. The system introduces three key improvements: (1) a semantic-aware user preference encoder that incorporates product attributes and category hierarchies using knowledge graph embeddings; (2) a context-aware graph construction module that models temporal dynamics and situational contexts as edge attributes; and (3) an efficient subgraph sampling strategy that reduces computational complexity while preserving structural properties. We implement the system using a distributed graph processing framework capable of handling 100 million users and 1 billion interactions. Online A/B testing conducted with 500,000 active users over 30 days demonstrates a 23.5% increase in click-through rate and 18.7% improvement in conversion rate compared to the production baseline. The system has been successfully deployed in a large-scale e-commerce platform, providing personalized product recommendations with significantly improved relevance and diversity.
